classification.difficultyReason: Find a population increase by decimal subtraction, convert millions to people and divide by five to find the average annual increase.

content.prompt: The population of Sydney was 3.9 million in 1996 and increased to 4.2 million in 2001. By what number of people did the population increase over the 5 years? What was the average annual increase?

answer.short: 300 000 people over the 5 years; an average of 60 000 people per year.
answer.worked:
Align the decimal points to subtract the populations, measured in millions:
$$\begin{array}{r}4.2\\-3.9\\\hline0.3\\\end{array}$$
The population increase was $0.3$ million, or $300\,000$ people.
$$300\,000\div5=60\,000$$
The average annual increase was $60\,000$ people per year.
